subject: Customer report: brief 'empty' responses during nightly batch – closure
content:
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@clearpulse.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 8 May 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: brief empty responses in nightly batch

Hi Laura,

We saw ~8 short/empty completions from Redwood during our nightly enrichment run last night (approx 02:00–03:30 local). The outputs are either a single newline or an empty string. Not sure if this is a model issue or something in our client.

Attached is a small sample (request ids & payloads) and one screenshot. Can you take a look? This hit our retry logic which masked it in prod, but we want to understand root cause.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior SRE, ClearPulse

Attachment: request_samples.json (stub)

We're starting a triage now. Quick asks that will speed things up if you can share them:
- Full request_id values (if different from the sample) and exact timestamps (UTC) for any affected calls
- Whether you were hitting a streaming or non-streaming completion endpoint
- Any client-side logs that show the HTTP status code and connection timing (timeouts, 502/504, etc.)

I'm looping in Ben (support lead) and Neha from Infra who will try to reproduce and pull the server-side traces. We'll follow up with a timeline and any mitigation.

Best,

Forwarding ClearPulse report — they saw ~8 empty completions in the 02:00–03:30 window (PST). Attached sample includes request bodies and the sample timestamps.

What we know / asks:
- Customer uses streaming completions for the enrichment pipeline (they indicated this in the payloads)
- Requests are mostly short prompts (<= 80 tokens) but happened during a larger scheduled job (higher qps than usual)

Can you:
1) Attempt a targeted replay using the sample payloads under ~same concurrency and model variant (gptx-2-large-v1)
2) Pull request_trace and kernel traces for the listed timestamps (if present)
3) Check routing: whether any fallback to a cheaper variant occurred during that window

I attached the sample file from the customer. I will tell them we aim to have an initial update in 24–36 hours.

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 18:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: brief empty responses in nightly batch

Laura / Ben — quick repro/update notes from infra side after running the replay & log pulls. TL;DR: we could not reproduce the empty outputs and there is no server-side error trace for that window.

Steps taken:
- Replayed the exact payloads at similar concurrency (simulated their job) against gptx-2-large-v1 and two adjacent quantized variants. No empty or single-newline completions observed across ~10k trials.
- Pulled request traces for 2028-05-08T09:50:00Z–2028-05-08T10:15:00Z and cross-checked token counts and latency distributions. All completions show tokens emitted; no kernel-level failures or segmentation events in the runtime.
- Checked routing logs: no fallback events from gptx-2-large-v1 to a lower-quality variant during their window. Autoscaling showed a brief CPU spike but within SLOs.
- Examined network edge logs for 502/504 responses during the window: there are two 504s from the customer's IP cluster at 02:09 and 02:37 local — those correspond to connection-level timeouts before the client received a body.

Attachments we added to this investigation:
- support_logs.zip (contains request_trace extracts, kernel metadata, and edge logs)
- investigation_timeline.csv (quick timeline of events we stitched together)

Preliminary conclusion:
- No evidence of server-side empty completions; data suggests client-side connection/timeouts for at least two events. Given the customer's retry logic masked the user impact, it's possible their client dropped or truncated the body in some cases.

Next recommended steps for closure:
1) Share the support_logs.zip and timeline with the customer and ask for any client-side logs for the two 02:09 and 02:37 timestamps.
2) Recommend that they include server request_id in their logs and, if possible, enable non-streaming fallback to capture the full HTTP payload for future repros.
3) If customer can provide any raw replays that still reproduce, we'll re-open and escalate to runtime team.

I'll keep the logs available for 30 days. If you want, we can offer a one-time usage credit since this impacted their downstream job (keeps relationship goodwill).

-Neha
Infra Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.example

-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@clearpulse.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@clearpulse.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 19:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: brief empty responses in nightly batch — investigation summary and next steps

Alex / Jenna — thank you for the sample and patience while we investigated. Summary below and next steps.

What we did:
- Replayed the payloads you provided under similar concurrency against the same model variant and observed no empty outputs (10k+ trials).
- Pulled server-side request traces, kernel/runtime traces, and edge logs for your reported window. Logs are attached.
- Reviewed routing and autoscaling behavior for the window — no fallbacks to lower-quality variants and autoscaling remained within configured thresholds.

What we found:
- No server-side evidence of empty completions (no tokenization or generation failure recorded).
- Two edge-level 504/timeouts from your IP cluster at ~02:09 and ~02:37 local time. Those connections appear to have been terminated before a complete body reached your client.

Attachments: support_logs.zip (server traces & edge logs), investigation_timeline.csv (event timeline), request_samples.json (original sample you sent)

Recommended next steps for ClearPulse:
1) Please check the client-side logs for the two timestamps above and share any HTTP status / socket traces you have. If you can forward any raw client-side capture, we will re-open and dive deeper.
2) If useful, enable inclusion of the server request_id in your logs for faster correlating next time.
3) Consider a short-term increase in client-side read timeout during your nightly job or non-streaming fallback to avoid partial reads during transient network blips.

Closing note:
- We could not reproduce the symptom on our side and have no runtime evidence of server-side empty responses. Based on the available data, the most likely cause is client-side connection truncation/timeouts.
- We're happy to reopen immediately if you can provide additional traces or replays that reproduce the behavior.
- As a gesture of goodwill, we've applied a one-time $1,000 usage credit to your account to offset any downstream retries — please see the HubSpot ticket for details.

Thanks again for raising this and for working through the investigation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
